kpis.label: Distribution (DCF base)
kpis.change: operating profit after tax, less ~26% retained

charts.title: Operating Profit vs Statutory Net Income
charts.annotation: Operating profit after tax is Mirvac's own distributable measure and the earnings base the DCF capitalises; statutory net income swings on investment-property revaluations and is not used in the valuation.

charts.title: Net Income vs Reported Free Cash Flow
charts.annotation: Neither line is the DCF's earnings base -- see Operating Profit vs Statutory Net Income above and the Distribution KPI.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Mirvac Group: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Mirvac Group: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Mirvac Group: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure.

For Mirvac Group: reported FCF is not what the DCF uses. As a developer-REIT, statutory operating cash flow swings on inventory and settlement timing (FY2026 OCF was inflated by roughly $500m of asset sales and capital-partner sell-downs). The DCF instead capitalises Operating profit after tax ($508m FY2026, see the chart above) less the ~26% retained and reinvested, which nets to the FY2026 distribution of $376m (9.5c x 3,946m securities) -- that is the model's true "owner FCF" here, not this chart's reported FCF line.

What to watch:

  • Reported FCF diverging sharply from operating profit (a sign of inventory/settlement timing, not underlying cash generation)
  • The retention rate implied by distributions versus operating profit

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Mirvac Group: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Mirvac Group: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Operating profit vs statutory net income
profit.content:
Operating profit after tax is Mirvac's own distributable earnings measure -- Group operating EBIT less net interest and tax, excluding investment-property fair-value movements. Statutory net income is the IFRS bottom line, which includes those revaluations.

For Mirvac Group: this is the earnings base the DCF capitalises at the cost of equity. Statutory NPAT swung from -$805m (FY2024) to +$677m (FY2026) purely on property revaluations, while operating profit stayed in a comparatively narrow $474m-$631m band across the last decade -- treating the statutory swings as the company's earnings would produce a nonsensical valuation.

What to watch:

  • Operating profit trend, not the statutory line, for the underlying business
  • The gap between the two as a rough read on revaluation gains/losses that period
  • Operating ROE on book equity (508/9,355 ≈ 5.4% FY2026) against the 9.5% cost of equity -- the reason the DCF's intrinsic value sits below NTA

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Mirvac Group: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Mirvac Group: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

dcf.base_sublabel: Operating profit after tax, less ~26% retained & reinvested
